note: District judges are appointed by the Governor in consultation with the High Court (Article 233(1), claim c30). Taught in the adhastan section and mirrored in practice question q33.
The Chief Justice of a High Court is appointed by the President (Article 217(1), claim c07). Taught in the gothon_niyog section.

Enforcement of Fundamental Rights lies with both the Supreme Court (Article 32) and the High Courts (Article 226, claim c21); the citizen's choice of forum is claim c46. Taught in the ekhtiyar_rit section.

Protector of Fundamental Rights = the Judiciary. General judiciary question (primary POL-04/POL-11), but this chapter teaches the High Court's writ enforcement of Part III rights (claims c21, c46), so the concept is covered here.

'Independent judiciary' appears as a (correct) feature of the Indian federation among the options. Taught in the swadhinota_pithokikoron section (claims c39, c40, c42, c43) and cited there in the text.
'Green Bench' (a bench hearing environment-related matters): the term appears in neither the Constitution text nor the NCERT Judiciary chapter used as sources. Source gap; not taught in this chapter.

The Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha enjoys the rank of a High Court Judge: the question is about the Leader of the Opposition's rank (Parliament, POL-09/POL-10 territory); a High Court Judge appears only as an option. Not this chapter's subject.
